clue.text: One is on right channel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece sitting on another means it follows it

parts.note: an ace is the card counting as one

explanation.surface: Someone claims a certain TV station is the right one to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on' places ACE after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a fast-flowing water channel, as in a mill race.

clue.text: Food for the morning in borstal is cooked

indicators.note: the morning abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged letters
something cooked has been worked over, so the letters of borstal are rearranged

parts.note: AM (ante meridiem) means the morning

explanation.surface: Breakfast served in a young offenders' institution has been prepared in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooked' rearranges the borstal letters as ROASTLB. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasted joint of young sheep meat is a classic Sunday dish, so it is a type of food.

clue.text: Church unit against wine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
anti means opposed to, against

explanation.surface: A congregation stands united in opposing alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany, an example of the drink.

clue.text: Pole keeping beer, oddly, in personal transport

indicators.note: the picked letters are set inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a private vehicle, personal transport

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word beer

explanation.surface: A Polish man drinks beer, strangely, while driving his own vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes B and E from 'beer'; 'in' places them inside CAR. 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the long wooden trunk tossed at Highland games, a heavy pole.

clue.text: Join forces for peace or to negotiate

indicators.note: to negotiate is to work things around, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two sides decide whether to talk peace or go on fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiate' rearranges PEACE OR TO, all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To work together toward a shared aim is to combine efforts, joining forces.

clue.text: Resentful in front of new one with wings

indicators.note: the first piece stands ahead of the second in this down entry

parts.note: bitter means resentful

explanation.surface: Someone feels aggrieved being upstaged by a newcomer who has flown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' puts BITTER before N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittern is a marsh bird of the heron family, and birds have wings.

clue.text: Weapon search

definitions.meaning: a long gun with a grooved barrel
to rummage through something hastily, often to steal

explanation.surface: A police hunt for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a firearm and also means to ransack a drawer or pocket.

clue.text: Small concessions for work on board ship

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so one piece goes between the letters of the other

parts.note: SS (steamship) stands for a ship
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Sailors are given minor perks in return for their labour at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sailors' perks; 'on board' is the container signal, as being aboard a ship means being inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a small gift or gesture offered to placate someone, a token concession.

clue.text: Programme like this on a spiritual leader and artist

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
the Pope leads the Catholic Church
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A TV documentary features a religious head alongside a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces. RA is a member of the Royal Academy, the London art institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama, a kind of broadcast show.

clue.text: Fake coins soldiers care for

parts.note: P stands for pence, British coins
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
to tend is to look after, care for

explanation.surface: Counterfeit money is what troops look after.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a British army unit; P is pence, the British penny coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to put on a false show, to feign or fake.

clue.text: Flounder when caught? One certainly does

definitions.text: Flounder when caught? One certainly does

parts.words: Flounder when caught? One certainly does
parts.note: a flounder is a flatfish; once landed it is in the wrong element, and a person in that situation struggles helplessly, that is, flounders

explanation.surface: An angler's flatfish struggles when it is landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' is both the fish and the verb for struggling clumsily, so the phrase fits the landed fish and the awkward person alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone ill at ease in unfamiliar surroundings, which a landed flatfish literally is.

clue.text: Snarl, seeing no good in the story

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for a story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A dog growls on finding nothing worthwhile in a narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarl' suggests a growl, but here it means a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl is a twisted, knotted mass, like a muddle of thread or hair.

clue.text: Pig styes?

parts.note: a pig's sty is an ugly sight, while a stye is an inflamed spot on the eyelid, so the phrase reads both ways

explanation.surface: A question about farmyard pens for hogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling 'styes' points to the eye infection; a pigsty is also a classic unsightly blot on the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsightly thing is an ugly blot, and styes are painful swellings of the eyelid.

clue.text: A damaging fall?

parts.note: a fall here is precipitation from the sky, polluted enough to harm forests and buildings

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a tumble did any harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests a tumble, but it is weather falling from clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted precipitation corrodes stone and kills trees, so it is a harmful downpour.

clue.text: Germany have the side? Absolutely!

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to own is to have
right is one side

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the German team has the better players, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means thoroughly or completely, as in 'downright rude'.

clue.text: Exaggerate past deeds only for starters

parts.note: over means finished, past

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the first letters of deeds and only are taken

explanation.surface: Someone advises dwelling on earlier achievements only at the beginning of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes D and O from 'deeds only'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate or carry something to excess is to take it too far.

clue.text: Unfashionable American ranch is fully extended

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
in US usage a spread is a large farm or ranch

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned US cattle farm covers a huge area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links. Spread for a ranch is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched open to its full width is spread out wide.

clue.text: Even a lord goes off carrying too much

indicators.note: going off suggests something going wrong or bad, so the letters of the phrase are scrambled

explanation.surface: Even an aristocrat leaves when burdened with excess luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' rearranges EVEN A LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Overloaded with cargo or burdens means bearing an excessive weight.

clue.text: Randomly read about mad cow disease, accepting argument

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone casually reads up on the cattle illness and gets drawn into a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here, not a reversal or container signal; 'Randomly' looks like an anagram cue but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to glance through pages idly, dipping in here and there.

clue.text: Plunder smuggled wine from Spain

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so ran means smuggled
sack is an old name for Spanish white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: Contraband Spanish drink is seized as loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is a historical fortified wine from Spain, Falstaff's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place violently and steal from it, to pillage.

clue.text: Be alert — a change is due and is liable to tax

indicators.note: a change being due signals that the preceding letters will be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to stay watchful because a tax change on property is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change is due' rearranges BE ALERT A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, property that can be assessed for local rates is subject to taxation.

clue.text: Camp entertainer who acted or played

indicators.note: played suggests performing a part, here also rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A holiday host is someone who performed or acted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ACTED OR. A redcoat is a staff entertainer at a Butlin's holiday camp in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: At British holiday camps the uniformed hosts who run shows and games wear scarlet jackets.

clue.text: Guns found in cells!

definitions.meaning: a group of artillery pieces deployed together
a power source made of linked electric cells; also cages for hens

explanation.surface: Weapons are discovered in prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures guns hidden in a jail; the cells are electrical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an artillery unit and a set of electrical cells storing power.

clue.text: Impressed and serious during final

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the end is the final part
grave means serious

explanation.surface: Someone was struck by how solemn the final match was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' reads as admiring, but it means stamped or cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressed into a surface has been cut or stamped into it.

clue.text: Checks to cover origin of narrow openings

indicators.note: covering means enclosing, so the checks word wraps around the letter

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Inspectors investigate where small gaps came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' gives N from 'narrow'; 'to cover' puts VETS around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vents are outlets that let air or gas escape, small openings.

clue.text: Job confronting a student of letters

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the job word stands in front of the rest

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A job interview where a learner faces a literature specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal relates to mail, the delivery of written correspondence.

clue.text: Ashamed to see individuals being taken in by suspended boss

indicators.note: taken in means enclosed, so the individuals word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: hanging means suspended
the head is the boss
ones are single individuals

explanation.surface: A suspended manager feels disgrace at seeing staff fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended boss' is two pieces that split apart around the individuals; the surface's suspended manager is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering one's face in shame is the idiom for feeling disgraced.

clue.text: Comic episode involving second gear?

parts.note: kit is equipment, gear

explanation.surface: A funny scene in a car where the driver is stuck in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' just links; 'gear' is equipment, not a car's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short humorous sketch or parody.

clue.text: Having had enough, was unhappy about note

indicators.note: about means around, so the unhappy word goes around the note

parts.note: sad means unhappy
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone who was full up felt miserable over a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' only links definition to wordplay; te is the seventh note of tonic sol-fa (do re mi).
explanation.definitionFit: Being full after eating means fully satisfied, with appetite gone.

clue.text: How you may need to start a song?

indicators.note: starting letters of each of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks how one should begin singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes the first letter of each of 'How you may need'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise sung in church.
